paper_title: High-Throughput Screening of Blade-Coated Polymer: Polymer Solar Cells: Solvent Determines Achievable Performance
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/ChemSusChem - 2021 - Harillo‐Baños - High‐Throughput Screening of Blade‐Coated Polymer Polymer Solar Cells  Solvent/auto/ChemSusChem - 2021 - Harillo‐Baños - High‐Throughput Screening of Blade‐Coated Polymer Polymer Solar Cells  Solvent.md

knowledge_points.content: The study utilizes the polymer donor PBDB-T and the polymer acceptor PF5-Y5, which is based on the non-fullerene acceptor (NFA) Y5 as the electron-deficient unit.
knowledge_points.evidence: In this work, the photovoltaic performance of blade-coated devices was studied based on the promising polymer:polymer system PBDB-T and PF5-Y5 as donor and acceptor, respectively.

knowledge_points.content: The highest recorded power conversion efficiency (PCE) for the blade-coated PBDB-T:PF5-Y5 devices was 6.43%, achieved using a CB/DCB (1:1) solvent system.
knowledge_points.evidence: Using the recently developed highthroughput methodology... the power conversion efficiency of the blade-coated devices varied from 0.08 to 6.43% in the best device... CB/DCB (1 : 1) [solvent system] ... PCE [%] 6.43.

knowledge_points.content: The polymer acceptor PF5-Y5 exhibits an electron mobility of 3.18 × 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, which is comparable to its small-molecule counterpart Y5 (3.82 × 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹).
knowledge_points.evidence: The electron mobility of the latter [PF5-Y5] has been reported to be 3.18 × 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ very close to the mobility of Y5 small-molecule acceptor (3.82 × 10⁻³ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹).

knowledge_points.content: ANOVA statistical analysis determined that solvent selection, specifically boiling point and Hansen solubility parameters, has a significantly higher impact on device efficiency (F-factor up to 110) than active layer thickness (F-factor of 6) or donor:acceptor ratio (F-factor of 14).
knowledge_points.evidence: Statistical analysis based on ANOVA shows that the parameters related to the solvent characteristics (boiling point and Hansen solubility parameters) are the most important factors correlating to efficiency... larger F factors mean larger impact in the final PCE. [Table 3: blade speed 6, D/A ratio 14, boiling point 110].

knowledge_points.content: High-throughput screening of the active layer was achieved by using a variable speed blade during deposition to create thickness gradients ranging from 30 nm to 100 nm on a single substrate.
knowledge_points.evidence: These thickness gradients were fabricated by linearly decelerating the blade during deposition from 90 to 10 mm/s... Typically we have obtained thicknesses from 100 to 30 nm in a single substrate.

knowledge_points.content: The high-throughput methodology allowed for the fabrication and testing of 648 devices using only 22 mg of PBDB-T and 24 mg of PF5-Y5, averaging 0.07 mg of total material per pixel.
knowledge_points.evidence: Using only 22 mg of D and 24 mg of A, we have produced more than 500 devices... averaging to 0.07 mg of total material per pixel, where each pixel has an area of 8 mm².

knowledge_points.content: Raman spectroscopy imaging identified that low-efficiency devices often contain micron-sized, acceptor-rich crystallites of PF5-Y5 that are detrimental to performance.
knowledge_points.evidence: The Raman analysis shows that there are indeed variations in the local composition, specifically at defects and/or crystallites, that are in most cases, very rich in acceptor. This is consistent with the stronger tendency to crystallize for PF5-Y5.

knowledge_points.content: Higher solvent boiling points generally correlate with improved PCE in blade-coated all-PSCs because slower evaporation rates allow for better morphological reorganization of the polymer:polymer system.
knowledge_points.evidence: The observed trend between higher boiling point and higher PCE could be related with the slower evaporation rates in blade coating depositions, which would allow a morphological reorganization of the polymer:polymer system.

knowledge_points.content: The optimum active layer thickness for the PBDB-T:PF5-Y5 system processed via blade coating is typically below 100 nm, likely due to microstructure limitations on charge transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: Even though in organic solar cells the optimized active layer thickness is generally over 100 nm using blade coating of PBDB-T and PF5-Y5, the optimum thickness is below 100 nm. Probably, this may be because the microstructure of the polymers limits the charge transport.

knowledge_points.content: Visualizing device efficiency within the 3D Hansen solubility parameter space (δD, δP, δH) serves as a predictive tool for selecting optimal solvents that produce favorable microstructures without requiring direct measurement of the polymers' solubility parameters.
knowledge_points.evidence: We propose the visualization of the PCE in the Hansen space as a tool to guide the selection of solvents in all-PSC... we did not calculate the Hansen solubility parameters of both materials... instead, we find clear tendencies when plotting directly PCE.

knowledge_points.content: The devices utilized an inverted structure consisting of Glass/ITO/ZnO/Active Layer/MoOx/Ag.
knowledge_points.evidence: We fabricated the solar cells using an inverted structure. The bottom transport layer (ZnO)... The top transport layer... and electrode (MoOx/Ag) were thermally evaporated.
